142880.overview:
The young sorceress Nikki, the court jester Fargus, and his side-kick Sid the puppet are the three main protagonists of this 3D platform game. While attending a "Wizards in Training" seminar, Nikki accidentally casts a powerful magic spell, which results in a giant monsters swallowing the whole village. The three friends must now travel to a place called "Wishing Engine", and be granted a wish to revert the world back to normal.

The characters each have a special movement to kill enemies with. The game uses floating camera angles through a vast Prince of Persia-style world. The goal of the game is to clear the various levels, avoiding spikes and enemies and collecting coins for extra lives.

Unlike most 3D platformers, Pandemonium offers only two-dimensional movement, rather than complete freedom of movement. The characters move along a curving 2D course within a 3D environment.

142882.overview:
Pathway to Glory is a squad-based tactical combat game set in the second World War. The game is semi-turn-based, meaning that both sides play their turns one by one as their action points allow, but all players on one side can move all their units simultaneously.

The player can equip the soldiers as he wishes, and in addition there are vehicles and turrets that can be captured and used.

The game has a single-player campaign and a multiplayer mode that can be played locally over a Bluetooth connection or globally in the Nokia N-Gage Arena via a GPRS connection.

142884.overview:
Pathway to Glory: Ikusa Islands is the sequel to Pathway to Glory, a semi-turn-based combat game set in the second World War. The player controls a small squad of soldiers, who can be equipped with different weapons, and who can also utilize vehicles and stationary weapons like turrets. This time the battles are fought in the Pacific theatre of war.

In addition to a story-driven single-player campaign, Ikusa Islands has a multiplayer game mode that can be played locally via a Bluetooth connection and globally in the Nokia N-Gage Arena via an GPRS connection.

142888.overview:
Payload is a 3D combat racing game. The plot is set in the future, on one of the off-world planets, where a new and effective fuel type called Furium has been found. Due to the lack of better prospects, player assumes the role of a courier who has to find and deliver the valuable minerals, and on the way back has to fight off gangs of marauders and other delivery workers who'd like to get their hands on his payload. There's a story mode in the game which is told through the comic-like cut-scenes.

What puts Payload aside from many racing games is an open-world approach to level design, instead of a set of fixed linear tracks. On those levels or arenas the player could traverse in a hovercraft, pick up the minerals, race or fight the enemies, pick up power-ups and such. There are 11 different "skims" as the vehicles are called in the game and 10 worlds to explore. The looks and loadouts could be customized between the stages.

Graphically it is a combination of 3D landscapes and vehicles, and 2D objects, such as debris or boulders on the map. Besides the single player mode, there's a four player multiplayer option via Bluetooth. N-Gage Arena features included unlockable vehicles, uploadable rankings and customizable race conditions.

142893.overview:
Pocket Kingdom is a strategic MMORPG set in the fantasy world of Ulgress. The core gameplay mechanic is combining combat units into squadrons and sending them into battle during which you have no control. Units can be equipped with various armors and weapons, and their AI can be customized for different levels of attack and defense. Winning battles earns you loot and items. The items can be combined with other items and equipment to create new items with special powers. 

The game can be played both online and offline. When online the world map shows other players which you can interact with by sending text messages and engaging in battle. Online also features an auction mode where you can buy or sell units, items and equipment. The main difference when playing offline is the lack of other players. The world map in both cases is populated by cities and dungeons. 

The culture of leet-speak heavily influences Pocket Kingdom. The combat units are constantly uttering leet-speak during the battles, and even acknowledge their own existence in a game. The plot centers around players fighting for the #1 spot in the rankings after some griefers were banned from the game.

142895.overview:
Colored Puyos drop from the top to the bottom of a well and the player must combine four or more with same colour to make them pop away. The game can be played in story mode against varying levels of AI, or head-to-head with another N-Gage using the Bluetooth connection. An exercise mode and a puzzle mode can help in mastering the art of connecting Puyos.

The basic gameplay is simple, don't let the well fill up before your opponent. Combining more than four of the same colour launches "refugee" Puyos into the opponent's well, filling it up and disturbing the combo buildup. Triggering chains of Puyo pops grants more points and more "refugee" Puyos, so careful planning is essential.

142896.overview:
Puzzle Bobble VS is an N-Gage-exclusive installment in the long-running puzzle series. Unlike most entries, it does not feature solo puzzle levels but (as indicated by the title) only the competitive variant of the game.

The game can be played in single-player story mode or as a multi-player game for up to four players via bluetooth connection. In the story mode, series hero Bubblen (aka Bub in most US releases of the series) must recapture six stolen diamonds from bad guy Drunk and his minions. It consists of six consecutive one-on-one stages arranged on a map of Rainbow Island. Three difficulty settings are available, with a special ending only becoming available upon finishing the hardest level.

Gameplay follows the standard template of the series: at the start of a level, differently colored bubbles fill part of the play field. The players control a launcher at the bottom that can be aimed in any direction and shoots bubbles of random colors. When three or more bubbles of the same color touch, they are removed from the field, with any unattached bubbles falling away. Removing bubbles adds them to the opponents' fields. After a while, more bubbles fill in from the top, pushing the existing bubbles downward. A player loses when the bubbles reach the bottom of their field. Special power-ups are available via a bubble gauge, which fills when removing a certain amount of bubbles at once. Once the gauge is full, the powers can be unleashed at the press of a button.

143103.overview: Pool Friction is a 3D pool game with beautiful graphics (for the time), realistic physics, and nice sound effects. It features multiplayer by bluetooth and various game modes.
